claims.text: A determination of clinical need is based on patient safety and medical necessity under the law
claims.quote: A determination of clinical need is based on patient safety and medical necessity under the law

claims.text: Makary quote on outsourcing facilities and clear clinical need
claims.quote: When FDA-approved drugs are available, outsourcing facilities cannot lawfully compound using bulk drug substances unless there is a clear clinical need

claims.text: FDA will consider submitted comments before making a final determination; final outcome not settled

claims.quote: For Immediate Release: April 30, 2026

claims.text: Notice published in the Federal Register on May 1, 2026
claims.quote: [Federal Register Volume 91, Number 84 (Friday, May 1, 2026)]

claims.text: Outsourcing facility could still compound from bulk if the drug appears on the drug shortage list
claims.quote: the drug compounded from the bulk drug substance appears on the drug shortage list in effect under section 506E

claims.text: FDA places a substance on the list only when it determines clinical need
claims.quote: FDA will only place a bulk drug substance on the 503B Bulks List when we have determined there is a clinical need

claims.text: Supply issues such as backorders do not count as clinical need
claims.quote: FDA does not interpret supply issues, such as backorders, to be within the meaning of "clinical need" for compounding with a bulk drug substance.

claims.text: Convenience (ready-to-use form) and cost compared with approved drug are not clinical need
claims.quote: FDA does not consider convenience in administering a particular compounded drug product (e.g., a ready-to-use form) or the cost of the compounded drug product as compared with an FDA-approved drug product when assessing "clinical need."

claims.text: FDA asks whether an attribute of the approved drug makes it medically unsuitable to treat certain patients
claims.quote: an attribute of the FDA-approved drug product makes it medically unsuitable to treat certain patients

claims.text: FDA tentatively found no basis that an attribute of the approved products makes them medically unsuitable; proposes not to include the three substances
claims.quote: This notice identifies three bulk drug substances that FDA has considered and proposes not to include on the 503B Bulks List: semaglutide, tirzepatide, and liraglutide.

claims.text: As of May 31, 2026, 990 adverse event reports for compounded semaglutide and more than 730 for compounded tirzepatide

claims.quote: One year after withdrawal of once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg and lifestyle intervention, participants regained two-thirds of their prior weight loss, with similar changes in cardiometabolic variables.
